payload.analysis: The task operates on 28×28×3 images with ~90k training samples and a moderate class imbalance (1.63×). Three architectural facts dominate the design space. (1) Spatial resolution is extremely small: a 7×7 stride-2 first convolution (as in resnet18) immediately collapses 28→14→7, leaving only 49 spatial positions after the first block, which wastes the deeper layers' capacity. (2) Channel statistics are highly asymmetric—means range from 0.53 to 0.74 and stds from 0.12 to 0.18—so per-channel normalisation is not optional; it is the single highest-leverage preprocessing step. The low overall variance (all stds < 0.18) implies that discriminative signal is subtle and concentrated, favouring architectures with strong local feature extraction and careful normalisation over architectures that rely on global context from the outset. (3) The dataset size (~90k) is comfortable for CNNs but tight for full-scale transformers, especially given the imbalance which effectively reduces the minority-class sample count. Architecture ranking: residual_cnn is the strongest default because 2–4 residual blocks with 32→64→128 channels exploit local structure at 28×28 without over-parameterisation, and skip connections stabilise training at this depth. tiny_cnn serves as a fast, low-risk baseline for hyperparameter sweeps. compact_transformer is the preferred transformer entry point: with patch_size=4 it yields 49 tokens, which is enough for meaningful self-attention while keeping the parameter count modest. vision_transformer is viable only if patch_size is reduced to 2 (196 tokens) and depth is capped at 4–6 layers; otherwise the token count is too small for the attention mechanism to learn useful relational structure. resnet18 is the least suitable: its stem is designed for 224×224 inputs and will destroy spatial information at 28×28 unless the first conv is replaced with a 3×3 stride-1 kernel. For the 1.63× imbalance, class-weighted cross-entropy or focal loss (γ=1–2) should be the default, and the validation set (10k) is large enough to monitor per-class recall without overfitting to the metric. The cited evidence (efficient transformer design, small-image representation learning) supports the conclusion that at this resolution, inductive bias from convolutional locality outperforms pure attention unless the transformer is explicitly compacted.
parametrization_priorities: Learning rate: start at 1e-3 for CNNs, 3e-4 for transformers; use cosine or step decay with warmup of 5–10 epochs
Weight decay: 1e-4 to 5e-4 for CNNs; 0.05 for transformer (AdamW decoupled)
Batch size: 128–256 for CNNs; 64–128 for transformers (smaller to stabilise attention gradients with few tokens)
Dropout: 0.2–0.3 on classifier head; stochastic depth 0.1–0.2 in residual blocks; avoid heavy dropout in early conv layers at 28×28
Class-weighted loss or focal loss (γ=1.5) to address the 1.63× imbalance; monitor per-class F1 on validation
For transformers: num_heads=4–8, MLP expansion ratio=2–4, num_layers=4–6 (compact) or 8–12 (full ViT); keep d_model ≤ 192 to match the small token count
For CNNs: channel progression 32→64→128→256 with 2–4 residual blocks; kernel size 3×3 throughout
Early stopping patience of 5–8 epochs on validation loss; track both accuracy and macro-F1
representation_priorities: Per-channel normalisation using the provided means [0.7405, 0.5330, 0.7058] and stds [0.1237, 0.1768, 0.1244] before any model input; do not use global mean/std
Preserve full 28×28 spatial resolution through at least the first two feature-extraction stages; avoid stride-2 downsampling before the second block
For transformer variants, use patch_size=4 (49 tokens) as the default; patch_size=2 (196 tokens) only if attention quality is insufficient
Add a lightweight spatial attention or channel-attention (SE-style) module after the second conv block to compensate for the low channel variance and subtle features
Use global average pooling (not max pooling) before the classifier to retain soft spatial information at 28×28
Consider a 1×1 conv 'bottleneck' before the classifier to mix channels without further spatial reduction
If using residual blocks, keep the number of spatial downsampling steps to at most 2 (28→14→7) to retain enough spatial context
Apply data augmentation (random horizontal flip, small rotation ±10°, mild colour jitter) to counteract the low channel variance and reduce overfitting on the 90k samples
risks: Over-parameterisation: resnet18 or a deep ViT on 28×28 images will have more parameters than useful spatial information, leading to overfitting on 90k samples
Token starvation: transformer attention with <50 tokens may degenerate to near-uniform mixing, providing no advantage over a fully-connected layer
Class imbalance masking: overall accuracy may look acceptable while minority-class recall is poor; always track macro-F1 and per-class confusion

Channel variance suppression: the low stds (0.12–0.18) mean that without per-channel normalisation, the model may latch onto the brighter channel (R, mean 0.74) and ignore the more informative G channel (std 0.18)
Premature spatial collapse: any architecture that downsamples below 7×7 before the final pooling loses the spatial detail that 28×28 images carry
Hyperparameter transfer failure: learning rates and weight decay tuned for 224×224 ImageNet-style training will be poorly calibrated for 28×28; re-sweep is mandatory

Validation set leakage risk: with only 10k validation samples and 1.63× imbalance, a few hundred misclassified minority samples can swing the metric; use stratified splits and report confidence intervals
Transformer training instability at low token counts: attention logits can become poorly conditioned with 49 tokens; use pre-norm, gradient clipping (1.0), and a lower peak LR than CNNs
payload.transformer_guidance: At 28×28 the token budget is the binding constraint. With patch_size=4 the sequence length is 49, which is below the typical 196–576 tokens where self-attention learns rich relational structure. Therefore: (a) prefer compact_transformer over vision_transformer—its reduced d_model (64–128) and fewer layers (4–6) are better matched to 49 tokens and the 90k sample budget. (b) If using vision_transformer, set patch_size=2 to obtain 196 tokens, cap depth at 8 layers, d_model=192, heads=6, and add a learnable position embedding (not sinusoidal, since the grid is only 14×14). (c) Add a convolutional stem (2–3 layers of 3×3 conv with stride 2) before the patch embedding to inject local inductive bias; this hybrid 'conv-stem + transformer' pattern is well-supported by the cited efficient-transformer literature and is critical at this resolution. (d) Use LayerNorm (pre-norm) rather than PostNorm for training stability with few tokens. (e) Attention dropout of 0.1 and MLP dropout of 0.1 are sufficient; avoid heavier regularisation that would suppress the already-limited attention signal. (f) Do NOT use resnet18's 7×7 stride-2 stem as a transformer front-end—it destroys 75% of spatial information before the first attention layer. (g) If compute allows, run a small ablation: patch_size 2 vs 4, with and without conv stem, to confirm the token-count hypothesis before committing to a full search.
